consensus_summary: Primary meaning is the eye as lamp of the body signifying spiritual perception, insight, and the moral/spiritual condition of the inner person (healthy/single eye = light/enlightenment; evil/bad eye = darkness); common alternatives are God’s omniscient/watchful eyes, the evil-eye idiom of envy/stinginess/greed, and lust/desire of the eyes.
book_summary: The lamp of the body revealing the light within; a good eye gives and an evil eye withholds; God’s fiery eyes are His righteous watchers that range throughout the earth and shine like the stars.
consensus_core_identification: eye as lamp of the body = spiritual perception and inner moral condition
book_core_identification: eye as lamp revealing inner light + good eye gives / evil eye withholds + God’s fiery eyes as ranging righteous watchers
boundary_disagreement: Book elevates the generosity/stinginess reading of good/evil eye and the fiery-watcher (plus stars) reading of God’s eyes into the compact primary statement itself, whereas consensus keeps spiritual-perception/lamp as the dominant core and lists the other two as distinct common alternatives.
rationale: Minimum cores overlap on the shared Matt 6 lamp image and do not contradict; the book simply synthesizes that primary consensus strand with two already-common alternatives (Prov good/evil-eye idiom; Zech/Rev divine eyes) into one entry and adds the ‘fiery’/stars precision. This is a real but limited change of boundary and emphasis, not a replacement of referent.
strongest_objection: Consensus primary often stresses general spiritual enlightenment or blindness (eyes of the heart, Isa 6/John 9 motifs) more broadly than the book’s tighter give/withhold + fiery-watchers triad.
